canonical_name: Existence of incomparable computably enumerable Turing degrees (source family; exact encoding open)
literal_source_claim_en: An affirmative solution to Post's problem.
source_attribution: Richard Friedberg / Albert Muchnik; 1956 (catalog metadata only)
statement_blocker: The catalog says only that the theorem affirmatively solves Post's problem. A second repository record and a versioned secondary source identify the two-incomparable-c.e.-sets theorem, but the primary definition/result passages, assumptions, translations, proof boundaries, corrections, and errata have not been inspected and independently accepted. The c.e.-set model, set-to-partial-function oracle transport, Turing reducibility convention, ordered binders, exact conclusion, relationship to the intermediate-degree formulation, foundation policy, and boundary cases remain proposition-changing choices.
domain_and_universes: Expected universe 0 over natural numbers or positive integers, with two c.e. predicates/sets and their Turing oracle encodings. Exact carrier, representation, coding instances, quotient-degree use, and universe context remain open.
conclusion: Expected theorem family: existence of two computably enumerable sets whose Turing degrees are incomparable, equivalently neither set is Turing reducible to the other under an approved encoding. Exact source wording and Lean conclusion remain open.

candidate_scope_not_credited.post_problem_form: there exists a c.e. Turing degree strictly between the computable degree and the complete c.e. degree
